correctness.rationale: For a fixed subset S of k indices, no edge enters those k columns with probability q^(nk), while each of k selected rows must use one of the n-k other columns, independently: intersection probability q^(nk)(1-q^(n-k))^k. Summing subsets yields exact falling factorial moments and PGF. Pairwise B_i covariance <=0 gives Var<=EW and Chebyshev for diverging intensity. For finite nonzero limiting intensity q->1 and fixed-k ratios tend to 1; factorial-moment determinacy yields Poisson. Both sparse windows and intervening regime follow from elementary uniform logarithmic estimates. Independent enumeration exactly reproduced all n<=4 defect histograms.

Uniformly moving probabilities outside explicitly stated regimes are governed by intensity, not asserted as sharper rates.
